name: Prakriti
quote: In all things of nature there is something of the marvelous.
paragraphs: Prakriti is Sanskrit for nature - though not nature as scenery. In philosophy it names the primordial source from which all form and change emerge. That's the spirit behind the name: nature as the original innovator, the first laboratory, quietly running experiments long before we ever thought to.

This is where new ideas begin. These posts follow original thoughts, untested experiments, and fresh perspectives - the kind that come from looking at the world sideways rather than straight on. Some entries will be finished ideas; many will be half-formed ones worth thinking through in the open. If a concept is exploratory, unproven, or simply curious, it belongs here. The throughline is discovery: treating every observation as a possible seed, and giving it the room to grow.

name: Nazarya
quote: A line is a dot that went for a walk.
paragraphs: Nazarya means perspective - a way of seeing. And that, in the end, is what an illustration really is: not a picture of a thing, but a point of view on it. The name is a reminder that the drawing matters less as decoration than as a lens.

This series is devoted to illustration - the visual work, and the seeing behind it. These posts share drawings, studies, and finished pieces, along with the choices that shaped them: what to show, what to leave out, and why a subject looks the way it does through this particular pair of eyes. It's a space for the image to carry the idea, and for perspective to do the talking.

name: Sāṅkhya
quote: If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough.
paragraphs: Sāṅkhya comes from the Sanskrit for enumeration and analysis - the discipline of understanding something by taking it apart, piece by piece, down to its roots. It names knowledge that is earned through depth rather than skimmed from the surface.

This is where things slow down and go deep. These posts unpack the fundamentals - the concepts most of us use without ever examining - and take them back to first principles, explained properly. Expect careful breakdowns, the why beneath the what, and the patient work of making a hard idea genuinely clear. Where Prakriti asks new questions, Sankhya answers old ones thoroughly. It's for anyone who would rather understand a thing completely than merely recognize it.
